messages.subject: Re: Multiple group analysis with longitudinal data
parts:
If you have individuals who only exist in one time point then you should only need to place NA placeholders in the time points they didn't answer, and your dataset should consist of one participant's response vector per row (NAs included). If you stack the participants and record time as a type of grouping effect it's ignoring the within-subject correlation, and would be akin to treating a paired-samples t-test setup as a one-way t-test (if that helps conceptualize the issues using a more common statistical test). The MML estimator in mirt is not biased by missing data (it's actually quite efficient) so long as the data are truly missing at random. HTH.

Phil


On Thu, Jul 30, 2020 at 2:08 PM Donisha Smith <dsmi...@fiu.edu> wrote:
Hi,

I wanted to know if my current analysis is feasible with Mirt. I have been reviewing the irt literature and have found that the best way to generate a frame of reference to analyze repeated data is to conduct a stacked analysis. However, having to of the same patients within one data set results in a violation of independence so to resolve this, it is best to randomly select one time point for each patient so that you create a file that represents the average difficulty across the time points without violating dependency. 

Currently, I have created a randomly selected stacked file in R and I want to conduct conduct DIF analysis to ensure my items are functioning similarly across my two time points. My question is, will setting the randomly stacked data as the reference group and setting the pre and post data as focal groups with free means and variances but anchored item parameters cause issues? My plan is to do this then to use Mirt's DIF function with scheme = "drop_sequential" to analyze DIF with anchors. Then, I want to obtain the factor scores using this model to generate the expected post scores of the pre and post condition. Originally, I was going to use the stacked file as a reference then split the pre and post data into four gender x time subgroups; however, I read that having different sized groups can result in type I errors.

So, is this feasible with Mirt?

Thanks!
